name: Panaetius
biography: Introduced a substantial element of Platonism into Stoicism and abandoned strict materialism; friend of the younger Scipio and a major influence, via Cicero, in transmitting Stoicism to Rome; taught that the soul perishes with the body. Stoic philosopher (already introduced in Ch. XXVIII) revisited here as a friend of Polybius and of the younger Scipio; his more political, less Cynic-influenced version of Stoicism appealed strongly to serious Romans, who still had genuine opportunities for political action that Greeks under Macedonian rule had lost.
